entities.summary: Quintus Marcius Turbo was a Roman prefect of the Praetorian Guard and a trusted advisor to emperors Trajan and Hadrian. Born into a prominent Roman family, Turbo rose to prominence through his military prowess and diplomatic skills. In 121 CE, he played a key role in the Roman Empire's military campaign against the Dacians, which led to the annexation of Dacia and the incorporation of its rich resources into the empire. Turbo's influence extended beyond the military sphere, as he served as a mediator between the Roman Senate and the imperial court. His legacy is marked by the numerous public works and infrastructure projects he oversaw, including the construction of roads, bridges, and public buildings. Turbo's life and career serve as a testament to the enduring power of Roman diplomacy and strategic thinking. As he once said, 'Militia et dignitas vincit omnia' ('Military power and dignity conquer all').
